_comment: Accepted-risk record for GitHub code-scanning alerts that CANNOT be fixed in
this repository's source. Consumed by scripts/dismiss-code-scanning-alerts.sh,
which refuses to dismiss anything not listed here. Keep every entry specific:
an entry with no path or line matches every alert with that rule id.
Two classes live here, both documented in
1. TokenPermissionsID — a true finding about a write permission that is
structurally required (SARIF upload / same-repo push + PR). There is no
code shape that avoids it, so the choice is dismiss-with-reason or leave
the alert open forever. The workflows already declare least privilege:
read at workflow level, the one write at job level.
2. SASTID — scorecard's SAST probe samples merged commits; commits that
predate code scanning keep it open even though CodeQL now reports a
successful github-advanced-security check run on every pull request.

dismissals.comment: security-events: write is the ONLY permission that can upload SARIF to code scanning; it cannot be expressed as read. The reusable this job calls declares the same permission, and GitHub rejects a run at startup when the caller grants less than the callee requests (startup_failure, zero jobs) - so downgrading this to read does not reduce privilege, it silently disables code scanning. See standards#451 and the in-file comment.
Same structural requirement as the caller above: the scan job uploads its own SARIF, so security-events: write is the minimum this reusable can declare. Workflow-level actions/contents stay read.

security-events: write is required for the CodeQL SARIF upload that branch protection's code-scanning rule depends on. A caller of a reusable workflow must grant at least what the callee declares (startup_failure otherwise), so there is no lower-privilege spelling of this workflow. actions/contents remain read.

Job-scoped contents: write, needed to push propagated git hooks into target repositories; the workflow level is contents: read. pull-requests and actions were removed as dead grants. Scorecard reports every write permission without evaluating whether the job performs the matching operation.

Job-scoped contents: write + pull-requests: write, needed to push the machine-written measurement branch and open/update its single recording PR. The workflow level is contents: read. Nothing else in the repository writes with this job's token.

Job-scoped contents: write + pull-requests: write, needed by the commit-back and pr-back modes that push a regenerated CHANGELOG.md and open its PR. The reusable never grants this at workflow level, and check-only mode writes nothing. Callers that only ever pass mode=check-only can drop it on their side.

False positive as stated: this repository runs CodeQL on every push and pull request and the github-advanced-security 'CodeQL' check run reports success on current pull-request heads. Scorecard's SAST probe scores its sample of merged commits, so commits merged before code scanning was enabled keep the aggregate finding open; no commit can be retroactively given a check run. Dismissing this does not disable the SAST check - it is a threshold finding, not a control.

Same structural requirement as codeql.yml and hypatia-scan.yml: this job is the caller of hypatia-scan-reusable.yml, which uploads SARIF and therefore declares security-events: write. A caller may not grant less than the callee declares - the run then dies at startup with zero jobs - so there is no lower-privilege spelling of this workflow. Workflow level stays contents: read.

Same structural SARIF requirement as hypatia-scan.yml: this caller job grants security-events: write only so the pons job in deep-recon-reusable.yml can upload its SARIF to code scanning. A caller cannot grant less than the callee declares without startup_failure and zero jobs; workflow level remains contents: read and the panic-attack job declares contents: read only.

The pons job is the one job in this reusable that uploads SARIF, using github/codeql-action/upload-sarif, and security-events: write is the only permission spelling that can perform that upload. It is job-scoped: the reusable workflow level and the panic-attack job remain contents: read, and the scan itself still fails closed on error-severity findings or an incomplete scan.
